newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro shares buck Dow dip, await key U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro shares buck Dow dip, await key U.S. data.

text.p: European bourses shrugged off an overnight drop on Wall Street to open higher on Friday but many investors remain sidelined waiting for important U.S. economic data for interest rate clues.

Uncertainty also affected the dollar in early European trade where it was trapped in fairly tight ranges after sagging overnight in Asia. The possibility of intervention by Japanese authorities continued to weigh on the markets.
The day's primary focus is U.S. March retail sales and producer price figures scheduled for release at 1230 GMT.

"The U.S. figures are clearly of extreme importance to the market. If these figures are stronger than the market expects it will increase the likelihood of a near-term U.S. rate rise," said NatWest UK equities strategist David McBain.
A Reuters poll of economists forecast retail sales to rise 0.6 percent compared with February and producer prices to remain unchanged.
"We will probably anyway see one or two rate hikes there in the next few months taking U.S. rates up about 50 basis points," he said.
The U.S. Federal Reserve raised its key federal funds rate by 25 basis points on March 25.
Rate concerns pulled the Dow Jones Industrial Average down overnight to 0.36 percent or 23.79 points at 6,540.05.

The dollar was also pulled lower overnight in Asian trading where it hit lows of 1.7172 marks and 125.55 yen after confusing comments from Japanese officials. Cabinet minister Kabun Muto said: "An artificial attempt to check a further slide by the yen may not yield any result..."
But the Ministry of Finance quickly distanced itself from Muto's comments saying they did not reflect official policy.
Muto is regarded as a senior figure but something of a lone wolf in Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's government, Japanese political analysts said.
The Ministry of Finance emphasised that the official view is that the yen's recent falls are overdone and the Ministry is concerned about it.

The dollar's continued strength spurred on German investors who pushed the DAX index up 0.34 percent at its Friday open. They see the weakness of the once-mighty mark translating into higher profits for the country's big exporters.

German carmaker Volkswagen AG, which on Thursday jumped through the important 1,000 mark ($581) barrier, surged nearly 10 percent in early Friday on the back of a positive business outlook for the 1997 year.
London shares also made a strong opening showing, with the FTSE-100 index climbing 0.34 percent amid selective buying.
French shares were more tentative as the CAC-40 index nudged up a slight 0.09 percent to 2,610.25.
CURRENCIES AT 0850 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7196 marks and 126.07 yen, compared with 1.7177 and 126.02 in late European trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0850 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 14.6 points at 4,327.8.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 11.51 points at 3,363.00
PARIS - The CAC-40 index was 2.28 points higher at 2,610.25.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 0850 GMT
Gold was firmer at $348.35 an ounce, compared with the London close of $347.85 on Thursday. Silver was two cents lower at $4.79.
